# Testing Conventions

Three layers, three purposes. **Do not duplicate coverage across layers** — pick the cheapest layer that proves the behaviour.

**This is not license to skip a component's own test file because its behaviour happens to be
covered transitively elsewhere.** A component with real logic (branching, prop→JSX mapping
decisions, event wiring) gets its own `index.test.ts`/`index.test.tsx`, even when the state it
renders is owned by a hook that already has its own test, or a parent's assembly-level
Storybook `play` already exercises the rendered result. Resolve the duplication concern by
**scoping what that file asserts** — mock the hook/child component whose internals are proven
elsewhere, and test only this component's own contract (given a state, does it render the
right branch; given a DOM event, does it call the right handler) — not by leaving the
component with no test of its own. Relying on a *different* component's story to prove *this*
component's contract means the coverage isn't discoverable from the component's own folder,
and can silently vanish if that unrelated file changes. See
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` for the
resulting pattern (mocks `useSubscribeSection` and `ZimmSubscribeModal`, tests only its own
render-branch/event-wiring contract). A component with no branching or decision logic at all
(pure prop interpolation, e.g. `BottomBar`) still doesn't need its own suite — the exemption
below for single-parent internal components still applies there.

| Layer | Tool | What it covers | File pattern | CI gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unit | Vitest | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms, hook behaviour in isolation | `*.test.ts` co-located with the source | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
| Component interaction | Storybook `play` | User-facing interactions in a single component (clicks, form fills, focus management) | `*.stories.tsx` `play` function | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
| E2E | Playwright | Full user journeys across pages, multi-region, integration boundaries | `e2e/tests/**/*.spec.{ts,js}` | Every PR (`qa.yml`) — desktop + mobile Chromium against localhost/dev API; BrowserStack multi-browser on `release/**` only |

> Higher-level project rules: [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Testing. Day-to-day file conventions: [conventions.md](./conventions.md). This file describes **how** to write tests at each layer.

---

## What to test (and what to skip)

Write tests where failure would be **non-obvious** or **costly to debug**:

- ✅ Data mapping: Contentful → component props, locale/currency transforms, SFCC payload → view model
- ✅ Integration boundaries: Global-e pricing/tax logic, checkout ownership branching, consent gating
- ✅ Complex state: cart mutations, consent state changes, multi-step flows, optimistic-update rollback
- ✅ Pure logic that would survive a refactor invisibly if broken
- ❌ Re-exports, one-line passthroughs, type-only helpers
- ❌ Storybook visual snapshots — Chromatic/Loki belongs in a separate budget, not Vitest
- ❌ The framework — don't test that React renders, that Chakra applies styles, or that React Query caches

---

## Layer 1 — Vitest (unit)

### File layout

Co-located with the source, `.test.ts` suffix, never `.spec.ts`:

```
overrides/app/utils/formatPrice.ts
overrides/app/utils/formatPrice.test.ts
overrides/app/hooks/useCurrency.ts
overrides/app/hooks/useCurrency.test.ts
```

Components use `index.test.ts` next to `index.tsx` in the component folder
(see [components.md](./components.md) > Components).

### Structure

- `describe` blocks group related cases; `test` (or `it`) for individual cases.
- **Arrange → Act → Assert** pattern, one behaviour per test.
- Test names describe the behaviour, not the implementation: `"converts AUD to USD using the latest Global-e rate"` not `"calls convertCurrency"`.
- Use `beforeEach` for setup; clear mocks with `vi.clearAllMocks()` after each test.

### Mocking

- **Inline mock objects** for isolated unit tests — define plain JS objects right in the test file.
- **`vi.mock()`** for module-level stubs. Mock the smallest possible surface: a single function, not a whole module, when feasible.
- **MSW** is allowed for cross-functional integration tests (multiple modules wired together). Production paths must never depend on MSW — see AGENTS.md > Rules > "No mocking."
- Do not mock the thing under test; do not assert on internal implementation calls when an output assertion would do.
- **Known gap: `ZimmIcon` throws under Vitest.** It imports the base SFCC icons barrel
  (`app/components/icons`), which has a top-level side effect (`AmexSymbol.viewBox = ...`)
  that fails here because SVG imports resolve to raw path strings in this environment, not
  components. Not fixable from a test file — the SVG transform lives in `vitest.config.ts`,
  Tier 1 test config (AGENTS.md Hard Rule 8). Work around it by mocking `ZimmIcon` at the
  smallest surface in any test that renders an icon-consuming component:
  `vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', () => ({ ZimmIcon: () => null }))` — or,
  if an assertion depends on an accessible name the real `ZimmIcon` would carry (e.g. a
  fallback `<span aria-label>` with no wrapping interactive element), forward the relevant
  props instead of returning `null`. See `footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx` and
  `zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` for both variants.

### Commerce SDK hooks

Hooks that call `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` (e.g. `useCurrentBasket`, `useCurrentCustomer`) need a `QueryClientProvider` and `CommerceApiProvider` wrapper. Build a small `renderWithProviders` helper in `overrides/app/test-utils/` rather than duplicating wrapper boilerplate per test.

### What NOT to write at this layer

- Visual rendering — that's Storybook
- Cross-page navigation — that's Playwright
- Real network calls — never; use MSW or stubbed hooks

---

## Layer 2 — Storybook `play` (component interaction)

### When to use `play`

Every UI component has a `*.stories.tsx` (see [components.md](./components.md) > Storybook). Add a `play` function when there is **interactive behaviour worth asserting**:

- Form validation triggers on blur / submit
- Disclosure (accordion, drawer, modal) opens / closes via keyboard + mouse
- Focus moves correctly through a flow
- A controlled input's onChange wires through to the rendered output

If the story is purely visual (renders different prop combinations), no `play` is needed.

### Pattern

```tsx
import {expect, userEvent, within} from '@storybook/test'

export const SubmitDisabledUntilValid: Story = {
    play: async ({canvasElement}) => {
        const canvas = within(canvasElement)
        const submit = canvas.getByRole('button', {name: /submit/i})
        await expect(submit).toBeDisabled()
        await userEvent.type(canvas.getByLabelText(/email/i), 'name@example.com')
        await expect(submit).toBeEnabled()
    }
}
```

- Always query through `within(canvasElement)` — never reach into `document` directly.
- Use **`getByRole`** with an accessible name as the first-choice selector. Fall back to `getByLabelText` for form fields, `getByText` last.
- Don't import `userEvent` from `@testing-library/user-event` — use the Storybook re-export so the action is logged in the timeline.
- **Exception — Portal-rendered dialogs (Modal, Drawer).** Chakra's `Modal`/`Drawer` render their
  content via a React Portal that appends directly to `document.body`, outside `canvasElement` —
  and this project's `.storybook/preview.tsx` configures no custom portal container, so there is
  no way to reach that content through `within(canvasElement)`. A `play` function asserting on a
  portaled dialog's content queries `within(document.body)` instead for that assertion, with an
  inline comment citing this exception (see `zimmDrawer/index.stories.tsx`'s `Large` story). This
  is the only sanctioned use of `within(document.body)` at this layer — every other query still
  goes through `within(canvasElement)`.

### What NOT to write at this layer

- Multi-page flows — that's Playwright
- Heavy API mocking — keep stories visual, push integration assertions to Playwright

---

## Layer 3 — Playwright (E2E)

### Workflow

E2E tests follow the **three-stage gherkin-first workflow** (see [.claude/skills/qa-generate/](../skills/qa-generate/SKILL.md)):

1. Claude (or any developer) drafts a `.feature` file with Gherkin scenarios
2. Lead QA validates in plain English — **no Playwright code is written until sign-off**
3. Playwright spec is generated only after the `.feature` is approved

This prevents "technically correct tests of the wrong behaviour."

### File layout

```
e2e/features/         # Gherkin .feature files — source of truth, reviewed by Lead QA
e2e/fixtures/         # multi-region fixtures keyed by SITE_ID
e2e/support/
  helpers/            # shared helpers (auth, basket setup)
  pages/              # Page Object Model classes (BasePage, CheckoutPage, …)
e2e/tests/zimm/       # generated Playwright specs, mirroring features/
```

Spec filename convention for story-backed specs: `SFCC-NNN_short-description.<priority>.spec.ts`
(`.p0.` runs in the Digital SIT gate on `release/**`; on a `develop`-targeted PR, `e2e-localhost`
runs only the specs relevant to the diff — see **Change-scoped E2E** below). Jira-less smoke
tests use `SMOKE-{area}-{behaviour}.spec.js` instead — see
[e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) > Smoke tests.

### Change-scoped E2E (`develop`-targeted PRs only)

`e2e-localhost` (`.github/workflows/qa.yml`) narrows which specs it runs based on the changed
files in the diff, instead of always running the full suite:

- Every spec must carry a Playwright test tag matching its Gherkin file's `@area` tag (see
  [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) for the tag list — `homepage`,
  `checkout`, `search`, `account`, `pdp`, `plp`, `integrations`) — and, per **BrowserStack story
  scoping** below, its `@SFCC-NNN` tag too: `test('...', {tag: ['@homepage', '@SFCC-142']}, async
  ({page}) => {...})`. Smoke tests (no Jira story — see
  [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) > Smoke tests) are exempt from the
  `@SFCC-NNN` half of this — `@area @smoke` only.
- `detect-changes`'s `Get changed files` step defines one file-path allow-list per area
  (`e2e_homepage`, and so on as new areas get specs). `Compute E2E scope` narrows the run to
  that area's `--grep` tag **only if every e2e-relevant changed file falls inside that one
  area's allow-list**. A single file outside it (a shared/global path, or one no area has
  claimed yet) resolves to `e2e_scope: skip` instead — `e2e-localhost` does not run at all on
  that PR (changed 2026-08-25, at the developer's request; previously fell back to running the
  full suite on every such PR). `qa.yml`'s inline comments are the source of truth for the exact
  path lists — don't duplicate them here, they'll drift.
- **This is a deliberate coverage trade-off, not a gap to silently work around.** A
  `develop`-targeted PR that can't be scoped to one area gets no PR-time E2E run at all — only
  unit tests / Storybook, plus BrowserStack if the PR references a Jira key with a tagged spec.
  Full/non-P0 regression coverage for that PR is deferred to the existing post-merge P0 gates
  (`deploy-test.yml`'s Test-tier gate, `digital-sit.yml`'s `playwright-p0` on `release/**`) —
  which only cover P0-tagged journeys, a subset of the full suite. A non-P0 regression introduced
  by a shared/global-path change can therefore reach `develop` before anything catches it. This
  was accepted deliberately to stop the full suite running on every PR touching a shared path
  (the single largest line item in this repo's CI-minutes usage) — revisit if it causes real
  regressions to slip through in practice.
- `release/**`-targeted PRs always run the full suite regardless of diff, unchanged — a release
  PR aggregates a whole sprint and gets the supervised, thorough pre-merge treatment per
  [releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md). This skip-instead-of-full
  behavior only applies to `develop`-targeted PRs.
- **Adding a new area's first spec:** give it its own allow-list group in `qa.yml`'s
  `detect-changes` job, tag every `test()` in it with the matching `{tag: '@area'}`, and add it
  to this section. Forgetting either step doesn't lose coverage silently — it just means that
  spec's PRs get `e2e_scope: skip` (no PR-time run) instead of the scoping optimisation, same as
  any other unclaimed path.

### BrowserStack story scoping

`e2e-browserstack` is Zephyr-linked per-story execution, not a general regression gate — that's
what `e2e-localhost` and the Digital SIT gate are for. It's split across **two** workflows, by
target branch (2026-08-25 cost review — see "What `e2e-browserstack` actually tests against"
below for why):

- **`.github/workflows/qa.yml`** — `release/**` PRs. Runs inline alongside the rest of `QA`,
  full suite, unscoped, always against the static `test` tier (no per-branch preview exists for
  a `release/**`/`fix/release-*` branch — see below).
- **`.github/workflows/e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`** — `develop`-targeted PRs. A separate,
  `workflow_run`-triggered workflow, event-driven off `deploy-preview.yml`'s completion (see
  below for why it isn't just another `qa.yml` job).

Both name their one job identically (`Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)`), which
`zephyr-results-sync.yml` relies on below.

**How results actually reach Zephyr (SFCC-751).** BrowserStack's own native Jira/Zephyr
integration cannot do this — it only supports US/EU Zephyr API regions, and this org's Zephyr
Scale instance is DE-hosted (confirmed via BrowserStack's Quality Engineering Insights setup
flow, which has no field for a custom Zephyr API host). Instead, `.github/workflows/zephyr-
results-sync.yml` runs after every completed run of **either** `QA` or `Cross-browser E2E
(BrowserStack Preview)` (`workflow_run` watches both): it reads that run's BrowserStack build via
the Test Observability API (`GET /ext/v1/builds/{id}/testRuns` — the one endpoint with a real
per-test `tags` field; classic Automate's `builds.json`/`sessions.json` has none), and for every
result tagged `@zephyr:KEY` (see [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md)), posts a
Pass/Fail execution to Zephyr. On failure, it also files a Jira defect against the `@SFCC-NNN`
story directly via Jira's API — BrowserStack's own "Report a bug" flow is manual-UI-only,
confirmed no CLI/API/MCP path exists for automatic-on-failure filing. Zephyr's REST API has no
attachment endpoint at all (confirmed via multiple SmartBear community threads), so failure
evidence (BrowserStack session link, error text) goes on the Jira defect, not the Zephyr
execution. See `scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs`'s doc comment for the full mechanism.

**Both `zephyr-results-sync.yml` and `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` only exist once merged.**
GitHub only evaluates a `workflow_run`-triggering workflow's own definition from the repository's
**default branch** — a copy of either file sitting only on a feature/PR branch is invisible to
GitHub Actions entirely (doesn't even appear in `gh workflow list`) and will never fire, no matter
what happens on that PR. This also means neither workflow can be tested end-to-end against a real
PR before that PR merges — plan around this rather than expect a pre-merge dry run of the trigger
itself (each workflow's underlying *script*/*steps* logic can still be exercised independently —
`scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs` locally against a real BrowserStack build,
`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`'s BrowserStack run itself via `npm run test:story` — just not the
`workflow_run` trigger). `zephyr-results-sync.yml` deliberately does **not** check out
`github.event.workflow_run.head_sha` — a `workflow_run` job carries real secrets regardless of who
triggered the original run, so checking out and executing a PR branch's own version of
`scripts/*.mjs` at that ref would let a modified script on the branch exfiltrate credentials
directly. It checks out the default branch instead (no `ref:` override), which costs nothing given
the above. `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` **does** check out the triggering run's `head_sha` — it
has to, to run that PR's own `e2e/tests/zimm` specs and `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs` — which
carries the same secrets-alongside-PR-code shape `qa.yml`'s `e2e-browserstack` job already had on
`pull_request`; acceptable only because this repo's branches are always same-repo, never a fork
(see [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Branch Rules) — revisit if that ever changes.

**Build naming.** `browserstack.yml`'s `buildName`/`testObservabilityOptions.buildName` are both
derived from the PR's primary Jira key via `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs` (`node
scripts/computeBuildName.mjs SFCC-751` → `3-SFCC-751-SFCC-T285 - <short summary>`, prefixed with
`Sprint-` by the yml template) — a live Jira lookup for the sprint number + issue summary, plus a
grep across `e2e/tests/zimm` for any `@zephyr:` tag on a spec also carrying that Jira key. Only
the `develop`-PR path (`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`) calls this script with a real key —
`qa.yml`'s `release/**` path has no single primary story, so it just uses the plain run number.
Either job uploads the resulting name as a build artifact; `zephyr-results-sync.yml` downloads
that artifact (via `actions/download-artifact` and the triggering run's ID) instead of
recomputing the name itself — it deliberately checks out `develop`, not the PR branch (see the
workflow's own comment), so an independent recompute there would see a different
`e2e/tests/zimm` spec-file set than the triggering job did whenever a PR adds or renames a
Zephyr-tagged spec, and miss the build lookup entirely until the PR merges. An earlier version of
this paragraph described that as a small, accepted drift risk from calling the script
independently in both jobs — corrected 2026-08-25 (CodeRabbit, PR #61): the risk was real and
guaranteed for exactly this kind of PR, not rare, so it's fixed via artifact-passing instead of
documented as accepted. The download failing is only treated as "nothing to sync" when
`e2e-browserstack` never ran for that triggering run at all (checked via the Actions API); if that
job DID run and the artifact is still missing, the sync job fails loudly instead of guessing a
fallback name that could silently miss a real BrowserStack build (CodeRabbit flagged this
correctly, 2026-08-25).

**Desktop/mobile project isolation — a real gotcha, not a style choice.** BrowserStack Test
Observability groups results by test *title* across what it calls "reruns," regardless of which
Playwright project produced them. A spec whose desktop assertions pass on `chromium` and whose
mobile assertions are skipped or fail on `mobile-chrome` — if both share one test title — collapses
to a single dashboard row showing only the *last-recorded* status, silently hiding whichever
result didn't "win" (confirmed against real build data, SFCC-751, 2026-08-25 — a build with 11
real chromium passes and 11 skipped mobile-chrome entries under identical titles showed
`passed: 0, skipped: 11` via BrowserStack's own API, not just the dashboard UI). `test.skip()`
does not avoid this — the skipped entry still shares the title and still clobbers.

The only real fix is to stop the "wrong" project from ever collecting that test at all, which
`playwright.config.js`'s existing per-project `testIgnore` already supports: the `chromium`
project ignores `**/mobile/**`, and `mobile-chrome` ignores `**/desktop/**`. When a spec has
platform-specific assertions that would otherwise share a title across projects, split it into
genuinely separate files under sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/` folders (e.g.
`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/desktop/SFCC-751_header-nav-site-prefix.spec.js` and
`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/mobile/SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js`) rather than one file with
per-project `test.skip()` branches — that keeps each test's title unique to the one project that
ever runs it for real, so pass/fail on one project can never be overwritten by a skip or a
different result from the other. Same-file-with-distinct-titles was tried and rejected for this
exact reason — the underlying `test()` call is still collected (and skipped) on the other project
regardless of what its title says.

**Access-gated preview URLs.** `BasePage.goto()` supports two optional env vars,
`E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME`/`E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE`, for a `RETAIL_APP_HOME` that requires a custom
header to reach at all (e.g. an access-gated MRT preview URL) — unset by default, so SIT/
production targets need neither. Not Didomi-specific; a generic single header pair, since that's
the one real case this repo has needed so far.

**What `e2e-browserstack` actually tests against.** Not the static `test` tier by default —
`test` only updates via deliberate tag promotion (see [tagging.md](./tagging.md)), so its
currently-deployed build has no guaranteed relationship to any given PR. On the `develop`-PR path,
`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` downloads the hostname `deploy-preview.yml` persisted as an
artifact on its own run (ephemeral `pr-<slug>` MRT target, deployed on every push to the branch —
see that workflow) and points BrowserStack there — so it's testing this PR's own code.

**No fallback to the static test tier when that artifact is missing (removed 2026-08-26,
CodeRabbit flagged this correctly)** — an earlier version of this job silently fell back to the
static `test`-tier `RETAIL_APP_HOME` whenever `deploy-preview.yml` failed or hadn't finished. That
let a develop PR whose own deployment genuinely failed still produce a green, story-tagged Zephyr
execution (and a possible auto-filed Jira defect) that proved nothing about the PR's own code —
the exact condition the fallback existed to tolerate was the one that made its result meaningless.
`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`'s "Resolve BrowserStack test target" step now fails the job loudly
(`::error::` + `exit 1`) instead when the hostname artifact is missing, whether that's because
Deploy Preview failed outright or succeeded but didn't reach the artifact-upload step. Same
principle [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md)'s Graceful Degradation section already states for
checkout/payment: never silently substitute a different flow, surface an explicit error instead.
A cancelled Deploy Preview run is the one case with nothing to fail loudly about — the job-level
`if:` skips the whole job entirely rather than running it just to hit this failure, since there's
no meaningful error to surface for a run nobody asked to complete.

**This used to be a single job in `qa.yml` that polled for `deploy-preview.yml`'s run to finish —
that design is gone, not just retuned (2026-08-25 cost review).** It started alongside `Deploy
Preview` (both triggered by the same push) and slept in a loop waiting for it, since there was no
other way for one already-running, already-billed job to wait on a *different* workflow's run —
up to ~17 minutes of pure idle runner time per push, worst case, before the real BrowserStack run
even started. (An earlier version of this note described tuning that wait down from a wrongly
inflated 70-minute job timeout / 40-minute poll to 40/15 — that tuning is now moot; the wait
itself no longer exists.) `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` fixes this at the root by being a
separate workflow, `workflow_run`-triggered off `Deploy Preview`'s completion: GitHub fires it
the instant that run finishes, with the run ID and conclusion already in the event payload — no
polling, so no billed wait, ever. `release/**` PRs were never part of this problem —
`deploy-preview.yml` never runs for `fix/release-*` branches, so `qa.yml`'s `e2e-browserstack`
job (which still handles that path) goes straight to the static test tier with nothing to wait
for.

- **`release/**`-targeted PRs (`qa.yml`):** always run the full `e2e/tests/zimm` suite, unscoped.
  A release aggregates a whole sprint's stories, so per-story scoping doesn't apply — Zephyr
  traceability still works, since every test carries its own `@SFCC-NNN` tag individually.
- **`develop`-targeted PRs (`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`):** on `Deploy Preview`'s completion,
  the job finds the open PR for that branch (`gh pr list --head`, one call, no loop) and regexes
  `SFCC-\d+` out of its title, body, and branch name — the same signal the GitHub-for-Jira app
  uses to link a PR to an issue, so this needs no Jira API credentials of its own (duplicated from
  `qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` step rather than shared — the two workflows have no other runtime
  dependency on each other). If at least one key is found, the job runs `--grep`-scoped to that
  story's tag(s) (OR-joined if the PR references more than one). **No key found → the job exits
  without running BrowserStack.** This is deliberate, not a gap: with nothing to attribute results
  to in Zephyr, there's nothing correct to run. It also re-checks `qa.yml`'s own `e2e`-path
  relevance gate before running — a single non-looping artifact download from that commit's `QA`
  run — **but this is a fail-open check, not an unconditional guarantee** (CodeRabbit flagged the
  distinction correctly, 2026-08-26): the normal path is that a Jira-tagged PR touching nothing
  e2e-relevant genuinely skips BrowserStack. If the QA-run lookup or the `e2e-scope` artifact
  download itself fails for any reason (the run isn't found yet, the artifact expired, an API
  hiccup), this step assumes relevant rather than adding a retry loop to chase the optimisation —
  so in that specific failure case, a Jira-tagged PR can still run BrowserStack even when its
  changes weren't e2e-relevant. Worst case is one avoidable BrowserStack run, not a correctness
  problem, but it's a real exception to the "doesn't pay for a BrowserStack run" claim, not a
  universal guarantee.
- If a key is found but no spec carries the matching `@SFCC-NNN` tag, `--grep` matches zero
  tests and Playwright reports "no tests found" without spinning up any BrowserStack sessions
  — a free no-op, not a failure, and not something that falls back to a full run.
- Every story-backed spec needs its Jira key as a tag alongside its `@area` tag (see
  **Change-scoped E2E** above) for this to work — the `qa-generate` skill adds both
  automatically. Jira-less smoke tests (`@area @smoke` only) never match a story key, so they
  correctly never run under BrowserStack — that's expected, not a gap; they're already covered
  by `e2e-localhost`.
- **Local pre-push equivalent:** `npm run test:story` (`scripts/runStoryTests.sh`) runs the
  same `browserstack-node-sdk playwright test e2e/tests/zimm --grep` command against real
  BrowserStack, so a developer can exercise their story before opening the PR. Pass the key
  explicitly (`npm run test:story -- SFCC-142`) or let it auto-detect from commit messages on
  the branch and the branch name — the same `SFCC-\d+` pattern, applied to local git state
  instead of PR title/body since no PR exists yet at that point. Requires `BROWSERSTACK_*` and
  the `E2E_*`/`PWA_E2E_*` vars in `.env` — see `.env.sample`. Manual, not enforced by a git
  hook — relies on developer discipline, not a blocking gate.

### Multi-region fixtures

Build SITE_ID-keyed fixtures from day one — Zimmermann has 8 storefronts across 6 regions (AU, US domestic, US international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME) and 11 active locales. Do not retrofit. A test that hardcodes a region or currency cannot survive the rollout.

```ts
test.describe('Guest checkout', () => {
    for (const site of SITES) {
        test(`completes on ${site.id}`, async ({page}) => { ... })
    }
})
```

### Page Object Model

Selector priority — **enforce in code review**. Select elements the way real users (and assistive tech) perceive them:

1. **Accessible selectors** — role with accessible name, label, placeholder, visible text. `getByRole('button', {name: 'Add to bag'})`, `getByLabelText('Email')`, `getByPlaceholderText('Search')`, `getByText('Sale')`. First choice — these double as continuous a11y checks.
2. **Semantic selectors** — standard HTML attributes when no accessible selector applies. `getByAltText('Profile picture')`, `getByTitle('Close modal')`.
3. **Test IDs** — `data-testid` only when the element has no semantic meaning or text content (dynamic containers, canvas elements, loading spinners, complex layout blocks).

Never select by tag name, class name, or DOM position. The priority order keeps tests close to user experience and minimises `data-testid` clutter in the DOM, while still allowing a reliable fallback where semantics genuinely don't exist.

### What NOT to write at this layer

- Pure logic — that's Vitest
- Component interaction in isolation — that's Storybook `play`
- Network-mocked flows — Playwright always hits real SFCC APIs (dev org on feature PRs, SIT on the release gate). Do not stub network calls in Playwright tests.

# TypeScript Conventions

TypeScript-specific idioms that apply to every `.ts`/`.tsx` file. See
[conventions.md](./conventions.md) for the base "TypeScript only inside `overrides/`" rule
and general cross-cutting conventions; see [components.md](./components.md) for how these
apply specifically to component props and hook signatures.

---

- **No `any`** without an inline comment explaining why a narrower type is impossible.
  Prefer `unknown` with a type guard when the shape is genuinely not known at that point.
- **Prefer `type` over `interface`** for component props, shared shapes, and utility type
  aliases. Use `interface` only when declaration merging is genuinely needed.
- **No non-null assertion (`!`)** without an inline comment explaining why the value is
  guaranteed non-null at that point — same reasoning as the `any` policy. Prefer a proper
  null check, an early return, or narrowing the type instead.
- **Discriminated unions for variant/state modeling.** When a value can be one of several
  distinct shapes (e.g. a basket item that's either a product or a gift card, or a fetch
  state that's loading/error/success), model it as a discriminated union with a common
  literal `kind`/`type` field rather than one type with a pile of optional fields. Lets
  TypeScript narrow correctly in each branch instead of requiring manual `? :` guards.
- **Prefer utility types over hand-rolled duplicate shapes.** `Pick<ProductTileProps, 'id' | 'name'>`,
  `Omit<...>`, `Partial<...>`, `Required<...>` — reach for these before redeclaring a
  near-identical type by hand. A hand-copied type silently drifts from its source when the
  original changes; a utility type doesn't.
- **`import type` for type-only imports.** `import type {ProductTileProps} from './types'` —
  keeps type-only imports from ending up in the compiled bundle and makes the type-vs-value
  distinction explicit at the import site.
- **`satisfies` over a type assertion (`as`)** when you want literal-type inference _and_
  a check that the value conforms to a type — e.g. a config object where you want
  autocomplete on the literal keys but also compiler validation against a shape. Reach for
  `as` only when you're genuinely overriding what TypeScript can infer (and treat that the
  same as an `any` — comment why).
- **`readonly`** on props and arrays that the receiving component/function must not mutate
  — particularly array/object props passed down from a parent that still owns that data.
  Signals intent at the type level instead of relying on convention alone.
- **Generic type parameter naming.** Single-letter (`T`, `K`, `V`) is fine for a generic
  utility with one obvious parameter. Once there's more than one type parameter, or the
  generic's role isn't obvious from context, use a descriptive name prefixed with `T`
  (`TItem`, `TResponse`) so the signature reads clearly without having to trace usage.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_resize
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab to test responsive layouts. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page
entries.description:
Get content of a specific Confluence page by its ID, or by its title and space key.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    page_id: Confluence page ID. If provided, 'title' and 'space_key' are ignored.
    title: The exact title of the page. Must be used with 'space_key'.
    space_key: The key of the space. Must be used with 'title'.
    include_metadata: Whether to include page metadata.
    convert_to_markdown: Convert content to markdown (true) or keep raw HTML (false).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the page content and/or metadata, or an error if not found or parameters are invalid.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be found in the page URL). For example, in the URL 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', the page ID is '123456789'. Provide this OR both 'title' and 'space_key'. If page_id is provided, title and space_key will be ignored.

title.description: The exact title of the Confluence page. Use this with 'space_key' if 'page_id' is not known.

space_key.description: The key of the Confluence space where the page resides (e.g., 'DEV', 'TEAM'). Required if using 'title'.

include_metadata.description: Whether to include page metadata such as creation date, last update, version, and labels.

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Raw HTML can reveal macros (like dates) not visible in markdown, but CAUTION: using HTML significantly increases token usage in AI responses.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_space_page_tree
entries.description:
Get page hierarchy for a Confluence space as a flat list.

Returns pages with parent_id and depth attributes for token-efficient
processing. Filter by depth to focus on relevant sections, or find
pages by title. Much more efficient than rendering full ASCII trees.

Use this to understand space organization before creating/moving pages.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    space_key: Space key identifier.
    limit: Maximum pages to fetch (start with 100 for faster results).

Returns:
    JSON with space_key, total_pages, and pages array containing
    {id, title, parent_id, position, depth} for each page.
    Root pages have parent_id: null and depth: 0.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_search
entries.description:
Search Confluence content using simple terms or CQL.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    query: Search query - can be simple text or a CQL query string.
    limit: Maximum number of results (1-50).

##########################################################################################
SFCC-874 Product Card Group with Lookbook – PWA Component
--- DESCRIPTION ---
As a Developer, 
I want a reusable 
product-card-group-with-lookbook
 React component built to the Zimmermann Design System 2026 spec, 
so that it can render an editorial lookbook layout across pages including Shop the Edit, PDP, PLP and any other pages requiring an editorial lookbook layout.
The component renders an optional section header (title + link), an editorial/product-shot image on the left (lookbook slot), and a configurable number of product card slots. The width ratio of the lookbook image to the product tile column is controlled by 
grid
; the number of product tiles is controlled by 
qty
. At 
qty=5
, four product tiles render in a 2×2 grid alongside the lookbook image or product. It does not own the product data or image source — these are passed as props. 
Props in scope:
Prop
Values
Notes
size
Desktop, Tablet, Mobile
Controls layout breakpoint
grid
3, 4
Controls width ratio of lookbook image to product tile column. Grid 3 = 2/3 image width; Grid 4 = 3/4 image width. Desktop only — no visible difference at tablet/mobile.
qty
2, 3, 5
Number of product tiles to render. qty=2: 1 lookbook image + 1 product tile. qty=3: 1 lookbook image + 2 product tiles stacked vertically. qty=5: 1 lookbook image + 4 product tiles in a 2×2 grid.
showTitleAndLink
true, false
Toggles the entire section header
cardType
Product, Editorial
--- AC (flattened) ---
 * Given the component is rendered with valid props, when it mounts, then it displays the lookbook image slot on the left and the configured number of product tile slots on the right, matching the Figma spec for the given `grid` and `qty` combination.
 * Given `showTitleAndLink=true`, when the component renders, then the section header displays both the title and link.
 * Given `showTitleAndLink=false`, when the component renders, then the section header is not displayed.
 * Given cardType=Product, when the component renders, then the lookbook slot displays a standard product shot image.
 * Given cardType=Editorial, when the component renders, then the lookbook slot displays an editorial/campaign image.
 * Given `grid=3` at desktop with any qty value, when the component renders, then the lookbook image occupies approximately two-thirds of the component width and product tiles stack in the remaining column, matching the Figma grid-3 spec.
 * Given `grid=4` at desktop with any qty value, when the component renders, then the lookbook image occupies approximately three-quarters of the component width and product tiles stack in the narrower remaining column, matching the Figma grid-4 spec.
 * Given `qty=5` at desktop, when the component renders, then the lookbook image is displayed and 4 product tiles render in a 2x2 grid to the right, matching the Figma qty-5 spec.
 * Given `size=Desktop`, when the component mounts, then it renders in the grid layout matching the Figma desktop spec for the active `grid` and `qty` values.
 * Given `size=Tablet`, when the component mounts, then the lookbook image renders full-width at the top and product tiles render below using the Mobile card size, matching the Figma tablet spec.
 * Given `size=Mobile`, when the component mounts, then the layout matches the Figma mobile spec using the Mobile card size.
 * Given `size=Desktop`, when the component renders, then `imageGroup.showCarousel` controls carousel visibility and `imageGroup.showSlideIndicator` has no effect.
 * Given the component is rendered with an empty or missing product array, when it mounts, then no product cards are rendered and no error is thrown.
 * Given the component is interactive, when a keyboard user navigates through it, then all interactive elements are reachable and activatable via keyboard alone.
 * Given WCAG 2.1 AA criteria, when the component is tested, then it passes with no violations.
 * Tablet behaviour – qty=5
 * The qty=5 configuration renders 1 large product card and 4 small product cards on desktop. On tablet, only 3 small product cards are rendered — the 4th small card is hidden. This prevents an awkward orphaned card from appearing on its own row, as tablet uses a 3-column grid system.
##########################################################################################
SFCC-801 global/country-currency-selector — PWA Component
--- AC (flattened) ---
 * Component configuration
 * Given the component is rendered with showDescription=true, when the drawer opens, then a contextual description is displayed beneath the drawer header; when false, no description is rendered.
 * Given the component is rendered with showLanguageSelector=true, when the drawer opens, then a Language section with radio options is rendered below the country list; when false, no Language section is rendered.
 * Given the component is rendered with variant="country-currency-selector", when the drawer opens, then the main content area renders the full country list grouped by region with currency codes alongside each country.
 * country-selector-dropdown atom (region groups)
 * Given a region group is rendered, when in the collapsed state, then only the region label and chevron are visible and no country rows are shown beneath it.
 * Given a region group header is clicked or tapped, when toggled to expanded, then country rows appear beneath the header, each showing a flag icon, country name, and right-aligned currency code.
 * Given the drawer opens, when the shopper's current country falls within a region group, then that group renders in the expanded state with the current country's radio pre-selected.
 * Drawer shell and interaction
 * Given the component is rendered, when it opens, then it slides in from the right on desktop and full-width on mobile leaving a small space open at the bottom, with a dark overlay backdrop.
 * Given the drawer is open, when the shopper scrolls the country list, then the drawer header and the Confirm footer remain sticky and the country list scrolls independently.
 * Given the shopper selects a country and presses the Apply CTA, when confirmed, then onConfirm(country, locale) fires with the selected values and the consuming page handles the redirect.
 * Given the drawer is open, when the shopper presses the close (x) icon or the backdrop, then the drawer closes without firing the callback and the prior selection is retained.
 * accessibility
 * Given the component is rendered, when a keyboard user navigates, then focus is trapped within the open drawer, radio buttons are navigable via arrow keys, and closing the drawer returns focus to the trigger element.
 * Given the component renders on desktop, when viewed on mobile, then the drawer is full-width and all interactive elements meet minimum touch target size per the Design System spec.
 * Given the component is rendered, when a screen reader user interacts with the drawer, then the drawer is announced as a dialog with an accessible name, all interactive elements have descriptive labels, the accordion region groups expose expanded/collapsed state via aria-expanded, and the search field (if rendered) has an accessible label.
##########################################################################################
SFCC-743 Product Card Group – PWA Component
--- DESCRIPTION ---
As a Developer, 


I want a reusable 
product-card-group
 React component built to the Zimmermann Design System 2026 spec, 


so that it can render a labelled group of product cards across multiple pages including PDP, PLP, and Homepage.
The component renders an optional section header (title + link) and a responsive row of ProductCard components (SFCC-236). It does not own the product data or navigation logic — it receives a product array, title, and link label as props. Whether the underlying data comes from SFCC merchandising logic, a Contentful-curated editorial slot, or a personalisation engine is irrelevant to the component.
Props in scope:
Prop
Values
Notes
display
3, 4, 6
Controls number of product cards rendered
size
Desktop, Mobile
Controls layout breakpoint
showTitleAndLink
true, false
Toggles the entire section header
showLink
true, false
Independently toggles the link within the header; only applies when showTitleAndLink=true
title
string
Section heading text
linkLabel
string
Link text e.g. Shop All, View More
Examples of usage: More from this category and Recommended for you on the PDP.
--- AC (flattened) ---
 * 1. Given the component is rendered with a valid display prop, when it mounts, then the correct number of ProductCard instances are rendered matching the display value.2. Given showTitleAndLink=true and showLink=true, when the component renders, then the section header displays both the title and the link using the linkLabel value.3. Given showTitleAndLink=true and showLink=false, when the component renders, then the title is displayed but no link is shown.4. Given showTitleAndLink=false, when the component renders, then neither the title nor the link are displayed.5. Given the section header is visible, when rendered, then the title is a semantically correct heading element and the link is a native anchor element with descriptive text.Accessibility8. Given the component is interactive, when a keyboard user navigates to the link, then it is reachable and activatable via keyboard alone.9. Given the component renders product cards, when a screen reader traverses the group, then each card is distinguishable and the group is appropriately labelled.10. Given the component is rendered, when tested against WCAG 2.1 AA criteria, then it passes with no violations.

# PRD – Regional Storefronts, Consent & Routing

_Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheets "Regional Storefronts", "Country to Storefront Mapping", and "Data Migration, SEO, GEO & URL". Last updated: 2026-06-19. SFCC site IDs and locale IDs verified against bkzk-002 BM (2026-06-13)._

---

## 1. Storefronts & URL Prefixes (REG-001 – REG-008, REG-043, DMU-013, DMU-016)

**8 independent SFCC sites across 6 regions in Business Manager:** AU, US domestic, US international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME. A MX domestic site is planned for 2027. EU domestic and EU international remain **separate sites** (REG-006).

> **Status (2026-07-10):** REG-005 is **updated** — the US is now **two separate SFCC sites**: a US domestic site (`/us/`, SFCC checkout only) and a US international site (`/en-ca/`, Global-e checkout only). This supersedes the 2026-06-11 single-site decision. Rationale: managing Global-e complexity is simpler with a dedicated site boundary; inventory pooling and reporting can be handled at the SFCC realm level. **New site IDs require confirmation in Business Manager** — `ZimmermannUSIntl` is the working name for the international site.

Each storefront has its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, and payment methods, configured independently (REG-002).

11 active locales across the 8 sites (REG-043). EU domestic and EU international remain separate storefronts (REG-006). US domestic and US international are now separate storefronts (REG-005, updated 2026-07-10).

SFCC site IDs and BM locale IDs (verified 2026-06-13):

| Locale           | SFCC Site ID               | BM Locale ID                     | URL prefix                     | Local currency         | Checkout owner          |
| ---------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ---------------------- | ----------------------- |
| AU (+ Oceania)   | `ZimmermannAU`             | `en`                             | `/` (root; x-default hreflang) | AUD                    | SFCC (REG-003)          |
| UK               | `ZimmermannUK`             | `en-GB`                          | `/uk/`                         | GBP                    | SFCC (REG-004)          |
| US domestic      | `ZimmermannUS`             | `en-US`                          | `/us/`                         | USD                    | SFCC (REG-005)          |
| US international | `ZimmermannUSIntl` _(TBC)_ | `en-US` _(confirm locale in BM)_ | `/en-ca/`                      | USD                    | Global-e (REG-005)      |
| EU domestic (EN) | `ZimmermannEU`             | `en-GB`                          | `/en-eu/`                      | EUR                    | SFCC (REG-006 dom)      |
| EU domestic (FR) | `ZimmermannEU`             | `fr`                             | `/fr-eu/`                      | EUR                    | SFCC                    |
| EU domestic (IT) | `ZimmermannEU`             | `it`                             | `/it-eu/`                      | EUR                    | SFCC                    |
| EU domestic (ES) | `ZimmermannEU`             | `es`                             | `/es-eu/`                      | EUR                    | SFCC                    |
| EU international | `ZimmermannEUIntl`         | `en-CH`                          | `/en-ch/`                      | EUR                    | Global-e (REG-006 intl) |
| HK               | `ZimmermannHK`             | `en-HK`                          | `/hk/`                         | HKD (SFCC price books) | Global-e (REG-007)      |
| ME               | `ZimmermannME`             | `en-AE`                          | `/en-ae/`                      | AED (SFCC price books) | Global-e (REG-008)      |

ROW also routed via `/en-ch/` and `/en-ca/` prefixes (DMU-013; see [dataMigrationSeo.md](dataMigrationSeo.md) for full URL strategy). AU configured as root with no locale prefix and designated x-default hreflang target (DMU-016, **Resolved** — the AU root remains globally crawlable because search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt from the human geo-redirect; see REG-009 in Section 4).

URL formats: product `/[prefix]/[name]-[colour].html` (the `.html` suffix is **preserved** to maintain existing indexed URLs — DMU-015); category `/[prefix]/[slug]` (no `.html`). Category URLs are updated for SEO consolidation (e.g. `/clothing/dresses`) with 301 redirects from all legacy paths (DMU-014).

Business users can manage storefront configuration in SFCC BM at both global and individual storefront levels (REG-010).

The US storefront supports all required US address formats; APO, FPO, and PO Box addresses are **not** supported (REG-012).

### Country → Storefront routing (Country to Storefront Mapping sheet)

The full per-country mapping lives in the source sheet; the FE only needs the routing logic:

- **AU (root):** Australia (default) and all Oceania — American Samoa, Cook Islands, Fiji, Guam, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Micronesia, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Northern Marianas, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu. NZ and New Caledonia get Avalara duty/tax; other Oceania destinations are DDU (REG-003).
- **UK (`/uk/`):** United Kingdom only.
- **US (`/us/` domestic):** United States (default) and **Puerto Rico**.
- **US (`/en-ca/` international, Global-e):** Canada, Mexico, and all other Americas — Caribbean, Central America, and South America (Argentina, Aruba, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Bermuda, Bolivia, Brazil, BVI, Cayman, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Grenada, Guatemala, Guyana, Haiti, Honduras, Jamaica, Nicaragua, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, St Kitts & Nevis, St Lucia, St Vincent, Trinidad & Tobago, Turks & Caicos, USVI, Uruguay, Venezuela, etc.).
- **EU domestic (`/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/`):** France (default), Germany, Italy, Spain, Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Austria, Ireland, Portugal, Greece, **Denmark**, Sweden, Finland, Poland, Czechia, Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, Croatia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Cyprus, Malta, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Andorra, Monaco, San Marino.
- **EU international (`/en-ch/`, Global-e):** Non-EU Europe (Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Albania, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Gibraltar, Greenland, Faroe Islands, Channel Islands, etc.) and **all of Africa** (Algeria, Angola, Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, Cape Verde, Chad, Comoros, Congo, Côte d'Ivoire, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Ethiopia, Gabon, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritania, Mauritius, Morocco, Mozambique, Namibia, Nigeria, Réunion, São Tomé, Senegal, Seychelles, Sierra Leone, South Africa, Swaziland, Tanzania, Togo, Tunisia, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe). Also includes Falkland Islands, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte, Saint Barthélemy, Saint Helena, Saint Martin, Suriname.
- **HK (`/hk/`, Global-e):** Hong Kong (default), China, Macau, Taiwan, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Brunei, Cambodia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Maldives, Mongolia, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Tajikistan, Timor-Leste, Uzbekistan. **Also includes "Australia" as a destination** — this is the REG-027 path for non-Oceania clients who select AU in the country selector (they are routed to HK, not the gated AU site).
- **ME (`/en-ae/`, Global-e):** UAE (default), Bahrain, Egypt, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia.

**Denmark routing is resolved → EU Domestic** (Country to Storefront Mapping sheet confirms; remove from Open Items).

> Geographic anomalies (mapping sheet): Falkland Islands, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte, Saint Barthélemy, Saint Helena, Saint Martin, Suriname all route to **EU International** despite being in the Americas/African geography. This follows fulfilment territory, not landmass — flagged for awareness; routing tables must follow the sheet verbatim.

---

## 2. Entry Routing & Mismatch Detection (REG-009, REG-013 – REG-035)

- **IP geolocation** selects the site on first visit (REG-013).
- **AU is gated** to AU and NZ/Pacific Island IPs only (REG-009). AU is the `x-default` hreflang and must remain crawlable, so it is never blocked at the network level. A non-AU/non-Oceania human visitor landing on AU is redirected server-side to their matched storefront before AUD pricing renders; if no storefront matches their region, fall back to HK. Search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt from the redirect — match by User-Agent against a comprehensive allowlist (Googlebot incl. Image/News, Bingbot, DuckDuckBot, AppleBot, YandexBot, Baiduspider, Slackbot, Twitterbot, facebookexternalhit, LinkedInBot, WhatsApp, Discordbot). Fail open: if UA looks botty but isn't matched, skip the redirect rather than apply it — false-positive cost is zero, missing a real crawler hurts SEO.
- All other storefronts use **mismatch detection** (REG-014): a country slide-out is shown on the first visit if the user's IP country does not match the storefront's shipping region (REG-015). Two CTAs: redirect to the appropriate storefront, or open the country selector (REG-016). A warning is shown that changing location may remove items from the bag (REG-017). Not shown if country matches (REG-018). Shown on first visit only — does not reappear after selection or dismissal (REG-019).
- **Country + language selector** available on all storefronts except AU (REG-020, REG-025). Countries grouped by region (Asia/Oceania, Europe, Americas) with currency display and search field (REG-021). Warning shown that changing location may remove items from the bag (REG-022). Country and language combined in the same selector; EU domestic offers EN/FR/IT/ES, all other storefronts English only (REG-023). Selected EU locale reflected in URL (REG-024).
- AU is gated and does **not** allow inbound cross-navigation from other sites (REG-025).
- **China** selected from any country selector routes to HK (REG-026).
- **Australia** selected from another storefront's country selector (i.e. clients outside Oceania) routes to HK (REG-027).
- Global-e checkout locks the shipping country — determined by country selector pre-checkout, cannot be changed inside Global-e (REG-028).

### EU language mismatch (REG-029 – REG-035)

When a user's GEO-IP country doesn't match the URL language on the EU domestic storefront, show a language mismatch modal in the current URL language (REG-029, REG-031). Two CTAs: continue in current language, or switch (REG-032). Country-to-language mapping (REG-030):

- France / Monaco → French (`/fr-eu/`)
- Italy / San Marino → Italian (`/it-eu/`)
- Spain → Spanish (`/es-eu/`)

Modal does not show when detected country matches the current URL language (REG-033), and is not shown for countries with no dedicated EU locale — they default to `/en-eu/` (REG-034). Logic applies regardless of entry point (Instagram, Google Shopping, direct URL, organic search) (REG-035).

---

## 3. Checkout Ownership

- **SFCC** owns domestic checkout for AU (REG-003), UK (REG-004), US domestic (REG-005), EU domestic (REG-006 dom).
- **Global-e** owns checkout for HK (REG-007), ME (REG-008), US international (REG-005 — now a separate SFCC site), EU international (REG-006 intl) — and for any domestic storefront when the customer's selected shipping destination is outside the domestic market.
- **AU serves Oceania (NZ, New Caledonia, Pacific Islands) domestically** via SFCC — not via Global-e. Avalara calculates duties/tax for NZ and New Caledonia specifically (REG-003); other Oceania destinations are DDU.
- Branch checkout ownership at PDP/cart, not only at the checkout page.
- **Global-e pricing via SFCC price books (REG-041, Confirmed 05-05):** SFCC holds all price books including for Global-e markets. AP21 feeds base RRP pricebooks per currency (AUD, EUR, GBP, USD) and fixed pricelists per Global-e market to SFCC via MuleSoft. A nightly job generates Global-e-derived pricebooks using FX rates and coefficients from Global-e. Global-e handles shipping charges, duties, and taxes at checkout. SFCC sends the complete cart in the target currency to Global-e. SFCC does **not** independently calculate shipping, duties, or tax for Global-e paths. (REG-040 was retired 05-05 — superseded by REG-041.)

_For checkout-specific frontend behaviour (redirect trigger, data flow), see [checkout.md](checkout.md)._

---

## 4. Currency & Tax (REG-036 – REG-042)

- Single currency per domestic storefront: AUD, USD, GBP, EUR (REG-039). No multi-currency toggle. (Open: Zimmermann would like multi-currency on AU domestic to offer NZD — not yet agreed.)
- Tax display: AU (GST), UK (VAT) via SFCC native tax tables, EU domestic (VAT) via Avalara (REG-037). The EU domestic site supports one RRP but must support multiple EU zone VAT requirements in the order payload. US domestic: prices excl. tax; Avalara calculates sales tax at checkout (REG-038). NZ and New Caledonia on AU: Avalara (REG-037).
- Sale pricing: was/now format. If price changes again after sale, only "now" updates; "was" is retained (REG-042).
- Prices shown in storefront currency on PDP, PLP, mini-cart, cart (REG-036).

---

## 5. EU Locale Billing Fields (REG-011)

The system will display locale-specific additional billing fields where required (e.g. Italian Codice Fiscale or VAT ID). **Open (REG-011):** confirm with Egaltine which other locales (e.g. Spanish NIF, French SIRET) require additional fields. Do not implement until confirmed.

---

## 6. Language & Translation (REG-044 – REG-047)

- EU domestic supports 4 languages: EN, FR, IT, ES (REG-044). All other storefronts English only.
- All customer-facing content (CMS from Contentful, product data from Product API) translated across EU locale variants (REG-045). CMS must accommodate translation-driven adjustments (e.g. button resize for translated CTAs).
- English is the site-wide fallback where translated content is unavailable (REG-046).
- Translation pipeline (REG-047, de-scoped 2026-05-25): the end-to-end configurable pipeline requirement was withdrawn. Translation occurs directly between **Contentful and Transperfect** outside the PWA Kit's concern; any SFCC-held strings (e.g. system messages, validation copy) are translated via static JSON files. No FE work required beyond consuming the translated Contentful payloads.

---

Get child pages and folders of a specific Confluence page.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    parent_id: The ID of the parent page.
    expand: Fields to expand.
    limit: Maximum number of child items.
    include_content: Whether to include page content.
    convert_to_markdown: Convert content to markdown if include_content is true.
    start: Starting index for pagination.
    include_folders: Whether to include child folders (default: True).

Returns:
    JSON string representing a list of child page and folder objects.

parent_id.description: The ID of the parent page whose children you want to retrieve

expand.description: Fields to expand in the response (e.g., 'version', 'body.storage')

limit.description: Maximum number of child items to return (1-50)

include_content.description: Whether to include the page content in the response

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page content to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Only relevant if include_content is true.

include_folders.description: Whether to include child folders in addition to child pages

9:## 1. Data Migration (DMU-001 – DMU-012)
11:- Product feed via MuleSoft from AP21 to SFCC covering ~1,600 active SKUs: names, descriptions, attributes, imagery refs, category assignments (DMU-001). Ongoing product sync via MuleSoft post-migration. **DMU-002 — Confirmed (status flipped from Ready for Sign Off, 2026-06-11).** The PWA-side contract is settled: SFCC displays exactly what MuleSoft returns for product data (JT 04-06), with AP21 as the master of record. Upstream sourcing (the first load draws from **both AP21 and PLM** via MuleSoft, with Magento-enriched data migrated after the initial load) sits **outside the PWA boundary** — the PWA does not enrich or compute product attributes itself, it renders the MuleSoft payload. The earlier RJ challenges (PLM/Magento enrichment) are upstream-of-MuleSoft concerns, not PWA blockers.
12:- Multi-region catalogue assignments and regional merchandising preserved across all storefronts (DMU-003).
13:- Registered customer records (DMU-004, updated 2026-05-25): **only email address and Omneo ID** are migrated to SFCC. Name, phone number, saved delivery addresses, and communication preferences are sourced **live from Omneo at login**, not held in SFCC. The previously requested 20-address cap is no longer relevant (addresses are not stored in SFCC). FE must treat Omneo as the source of customer profile data post-login; degrade gracefully if Omneo is unreachable.
14:- **Customer passwords are not migrated** — customers must reset on first login (DMU-005). See AGENTS.md "Magento password migration" gotcha.
15:- Saved payment card details are **not** migrated; customers re-enter at next purchase (DMU-006).
16:- Historical order records are **not** migrated into SFCC. Order history is accessed via NewStore **through MuleSoft** where customer identifiers match across online and in-store channels (DMU-007, **Confirmed 2026-06-11** — status flipped from Ready for Sign Off). The PWA displays exactly what MuleSoft returns for customer order history (JT 04-06); no order data is held in SFCC. ⚠️ Source-of-truth flag retained: the requirement text + JT name **NewStore via MuleSoft**, while an RJ comment says **"Order history will come from Omneo"** — the upstream source (NewStore vs Omneo behind MuleSoft) is out of the PWA boundary but remains unreconciled; see Open Items. For the ME storefront, only online orders appear in My Account order history; the orders API returns the most recent 50 orders held in NewStore, and until NewStore transitions in ME only online orders are visible — no FE customisation required to filter retail orders (DMU-008, Ready for Sign Off 2026-05-25).

18:- Product images and digital assets (DMU-010, de-scoped 2026-05-25): **out of scope for migration.** Images and assets are stored and served from Contentful — there is no CDN migration, no asset URL rewrite, and no 301 redirects for asset URLs.
